proof_status.scope: The specific dyadic vector-word phase recurrence, least periods, and a uniform O(P) native extractor with raw setup and output.

Linear-time full normalization for the stated phase on canonical dyadic banks is equivalent to canonical word transposition at all dimensions.

review_basis: Integration review against previously independently reviewed phase-extraction and normalizer-equivalence arguments; no new independent review claimed for this manuscript revision.
findings: The vector-polynomial selector retains the boundary word needed for the second leading coefficient; zero, fixed, and short-period columns are handled explicitly.
The phase recurrence is equivariant with the exact least period and yields a uniform fixed-tape O(P) schedule, including nested metadata, raw setup, resets, and output.
The least-significant marker fixes the exact phase origin independently of all higher payload lanes.
The forward reduction uses the correctly signed marked column shear, canonical width, full dyadic transpose before cropping, and a normalizer call of less than 32P bits for arbitrary dimensions.
The converse pays input-head resets, both transpose simulations, row rotations, and final output; its bound allows constant-factor simulation overhead.
The sibling identity and explicit counterexample explain the remaining full-payload obligation without claiming a general lower bound.
All three additional numbered results are explicitly marked not formalized; blanket Lean-coverage claims have been removed.
The final PDF has no clipping, overlaps, unresolved references, or LaTeX box warnings; the contents fit on the title page.
